title: Deriving the Schur-complement criterion by square completion
audience: A reader who can multiply real matrices and block vectors, transpose products, and complete a scalar square. Positive definiteness and the square-matrix kernel test are refreshed explicitly. No prior Schur-complement formula or invariance under congruence is assumed.
reader_goals: Derive the shift K=A^{-1}B by matching the mixed term, then reproduce the complete block square expansion.
Use the inverse coordinate map to prove sufficiency and a universally quantified cancellation vector to prove necessity.
Compute the scalar example A=2, B=1, C=1 and identify the failed sign step for A=-1, B=0, C=1; distinguish that counterexample from the unaddressed singular case.
prerequisites: Assumed: multiply compatible real matrices and block vectors, transpose a product, and recognize that a real scalar equals its transpose.
Assumed: expand a scalar square and collect coefficients; section 2 repeats the specific calculation used.
Refreshable: a real symmetric H is positive definite exactly when v^T H v>0 for every nonzero real v; this is stated with the goal theorem.
Refreshable imported input: a square linear map on a finite-dimensional vector space is invertible if its kernel is zero; used only to obtain A^{-1} from A>0.
Bridge-required: construct the block shift and residual S by explicit expansion, prove its inverse map, and track nonzero vectors. Both required result nodes are selected in full.

selections.reason: The full goal and both directions of its proof are the lecture task; square completion and nonzero-vector control are its two consumed inputs.
Execute the recorded scalar positive model and the negative-block counterexample; state the singular case only as noncoverage.
Prove both inverse compositions and use nonzero-pair preservation precisely in the sufficiency argument.
Build the exact identity by matching AK=B, checking dimensions and symmetry, and expanding all four terms before applying it.

omissions.reason: The lecture teaches the square-completion construction completely. A separate congruence formulation is not needed to execute this method, so its alternative matrix statement is omitted.

required_steps: Expand the square with A symmetric and invertible.
Use the invertible change of variables for sufficiency.
Choose x=-A^{-1}By for every nonzero y to prove necessity.
